script: I walked home, a 7th grader ambushed me—what happened next shocked everyone.. I was a third‑grade giant, glasses on, moving into a new town. Every day I walked the same two‑thirds of a mile home from that mixed elementary‑junior‑high building. The big kids usually kept to their own side, ignoring us little ones, but once in a while a seventh‑grader would pop up and try to boss us around. That day, as I trudged past the corner bush, a seventh‑grader—let's call him "The Bully" for now—jumped out like a bad dream and shoved me for no reason but because he could. I felt trapped, like my life was on the line. I didn't know how to punch properly, but I swung my umbrella like a puppy with a stick. I landed two or three thwacks before the fight ended in two minutes. He ran away. I walked home, brain buzzing, scrolling through after‑school specials to calm down. Later that evening, The Bully's mom called my mom, claiming I was picking on her son, endlessly bullying him. "I don't recognize your son's name," my mom said. "Is he in the other third‑grade class?" The mom sighed, "Your son is in third grade? I am sorry to have bothered you." She hung up. The Bully never came near me again.
